It recommends MinGit, taken directly from Git for Windows releases, as the manager's source, and the standard installer for client machines that a person will use directly. The git-scm.com download page does not list MinGit, so the recommendation rests on the release itself, whose checksums and signed tag make it verifiable. Three defaults in MinGit's system configuration need a deliberate decision before the manager ships. ## Sources and Acknowledgements The comparison applies *Universal Cake Evaluation Metrics* version 0.5.1 ([Steel, 2026](#apa-uc-metrics-reference)). The options come from the git-scm.com Windows download page ([Git Project, n.d.](#apa-gitscm-windows-reference)) and the Git for Windows 2.56.0.2 release behind it ([Git for Windows Project, 2026](#apa-gfw-release-reference)). Support periods come from the Git for Windows FAQ and its 32-bit support page. `MinGit-2.56.0.2-64-bit.zip` was downloaded, hashed, and unpacked on Linux to inspect its layout and configuration; no Windows binary was run. The evaluation was prepared with AI assistance from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). ## Scope The subject is Git for Windows 2.56.0.2, released on 2026-10-05, in each of the forms it is offered. Git's own behaviour, and Git on Linux and macOS, are out of scope; for those platforms, dugite-native remains the candidate, pending its own entry. Network behaviour and accessibility of the Windows builds were not tested, since nothing was run on Windows. ## The options | Option | Artifact | What it is | Use | |---|---|---|---| | MinGit | `MinGit-2.56.0.2-64-bit.zip`, also ARM64 and 32-bit | Git for Windows' minimal build for applications that bundle Git: `git.exe` and its helpers, Git Credential Manager, no Bash, no GUI tools. 39.8 MB zip, 93 MB unpacked (verified) | osat-manager-git | | MinGit, busybox variant | `MinGit-2.56.0.2-busybox-64-bit.zip`, also ARM64 and 32-bit | MinGit with BusyBox in place of the standard Unix tools; smaller, less compatible | None | | PortableGit | `PortableGit-2.56.0.2-64-bit.7z.exe`, also ARM64 | Full Git for Windows, including Git Bash, unpacked into any folder with no registry or PATH changes; a self-extracting 7-Zip archive that 7-Zip can open without running it | Optional full variant for the manager | | Full archive | `Git-2.56.0.2-64-bit.tar.bz2`, also ARM64 | The full Git as a plain archive | Alternative to PortableGit | | Standalone installer | `Git-2.56.0.2-64-bit.exe`, also ARM64 | Full Git for Windows with Git Bash, Git GUI, gitk, Explorer menus, and PATH changes | Client machines, git-cola | | winget | `winget install --id Git.Git -e --source winget` | The standalone installer, through Microsoft's package manager | Client setup where winget is present | | Build from source | Git for Windows repository | Compile it yourself | None | The git-scm.com page lists only the installer, PortableGit, winget, and source. MinGit, its busybox variants, and the full archives appear only on the release. ## The decisive observation The osat-manager pattern needs an artifact it can download, verify against a published checksum, unpack into a versioned directory, and point an alias at, with no installer and no system changes. MinGit is exactly that, and it is published by Git for Windows itself for this purpose. The installer and winget fail the pattern by design, since they decide where things go. PortableGit fits, but carries Git Bash and much more than a manager needs, so it suits an optional "full" variant rather than the default. dugite-native, the other candidate surveyed earlier, builds its Windows packages by repackaging MinGit. Taking MinGit at its source removes GitHub Desktop's packaging from the Windows dependency chain without losing anything. ## Gates for Git for Windows | Gate | Result | Evidence | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Telemetry or content exposure that cannot be disabled | Pass | Inferred | Git has no telemetry. Git Credential Manager contacts a hosting service only when credentials are requested for it. Not traced on Windows | | A licence incompatible with the project | Pass, for use | Verified | Git is GPL-2.0-only; the bundled `LICENSE.txt` states that only version 2 applies. Using MinGit raises no issue, and redistributing it carries the GPL's usual source obligations; Git's code cannot be combined into AGPL-3.0-or-later or GPL-3.0-or-later works | | Failure of the accessibility floor | Pass | Inferred | MinGit is a command-line tool with no interface of its own. The installer's accessibility was not tested | | No exit | Pass | Verified | Repositories are plain Git. Removing MinGit means deleting its directory | ## Verification The release notes carry a SHA-256 table covering every asset, the release tag is GPG-signed by the Git for Windows maintainer, and the executables carry Authenticode signatures (claimed by the release page). The downloaded MinGit zip hashed to `da35e72aa21c005a5a0d298cfbae110bc1609a815730ea0dde84b01a1b3cd3be`, matching the release notes (verified). The git-scm.com page itself publishes no checksums. The table is markdown inside the release notes, not a SHA256SUMS file, so the manager must parse it, unlike osat-manager-python, which reads python-build-standalone's SHA256SUMS. GitHub's release API may report a per-asset digest, which would be simpler; that could not be checked here and should be confirmed when the manager is built. ## Older systems Git for Windows supports Windows 8.1 and later, on x64 and ARM64 ([Git for Windows Project, n.d.-a](#apa-gfw-faq-reference)). Older systems can only run frozen releases. | System | Last Git for Windows release | |---|---| | Windows 7 and 8 | 2.46.2 | | Windows Vista and Server 2008 | 2.37.1 | | 32-bit, installer and PortableGit | 2.48.1 | | 32-bit, MinGit only | Supported until April 2029 | The 32-bit dates come from the project's support page ([Git for Windows Project, n.d.-b](#apa-gfw-32bit-reference)). A manager could pin 2.46.2 for a Windows 7 client, as the psutil entry suggests pinning 7.2.x for older Python, but that machine gets no further Git security fixes. Client-facing guidance should say so plainly. ## Recommendation | Option | Ring | For | |---|---|---| | MinGit, from Git for Windows releases | Trial | osat-manager-git's Windows source | | PortableGit | Assess | An optional full variant of the manager, for users who want Git Bash | | Standalone installer, or winget | Assess | Client machines a person uses directly, and git-cola, whose README asks for it | | MinGit busybox variants | Hold | Less compatible, no offsetting benefit | | Building from source | Hold | The official builds already meet the need | | Frozen releases for Windows 7, 8, or Vista | Hold | Only as a declared bridge, with the security cost stated | MinGit moves to Adopt when osat-manager-git installs, switches, and removes it end to end on real Windows hardware, with these decisions made and recorded in its proposal: - **Line endings.** MinGit's system configuration sets `core.autocrlf = true`. For SAT content repositories shared between Linux and Windows, decide whether the manager keeps this default or sets `autocrlf` per repository, preferably with a `.gitattributes` policy in the repositories themselves. - **Git LFS.** The same configuration declares the `lfs` filter with `required = true`, but MinGit ships no `git-lfs` executable (verified). A checkout of any repository that uses LFS will fail. The manager should either install Git LFS beside MinGit or tell the user plainly. - **Inherited configuration.** MinGit's system configuration includes `C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig` and its 32-bit counterpart, so on a machine that also has a full Git for Windows install, MinGit inherits that install's settings. The manager should document this or override it. - **Paths.** The 2.56 layout places Git's runtime under `ucrt64`, after a migration from `mingw64`. Aliases should target `cmd\git.exe`, the stable entry point, rather than paths inside the runtime directory. ## Flip conditions - If Git for Windows stops publishing 64-bit MinGit, the manager falls back to the full `tar.bz2` archive, which needs no installer either. - If users mostly want Git Bash, PortableGit becomes the default and MinGit the minimal option. - If checksum parsing from release notes proves fragile, and no API digest is available, verify against the signed tag by building, or pin by hash per version as osat-manager-python's archive already allows. ## Relationship to project This entry gives osat-manager-git its Windows half. On Linux and macOS the candidate remains dugite-native, whose builds need relocation variables in the alias wrapper, link the system's libcurl for HTTPS, and require glibc 2.34; that candidate needs its own entry. git-cola, evaluated separately, needs Git on the path and would be a natural consumer of the manager. ## Status notes - Last reviewed: 2026-10-11 - In assess: the automated pass recommends MinGit for Trial as the manager's Windows source. What moves it to Adopt is the manager working end to end on real Windows, with the four decisions above recorded in its proposal. - Re-review triggers: a change in how Git for Windows publishes checksums, any change to MinGit's default system configuration, and the end of 32-bit MinGit in April 2029. ## License This document, *Git on Windows, Options for osat-manager-git*, by **Christopher Steel**, with AI assistance from **Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)**, is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html). ## Resources ### Evaluation framework - [Universal Cake Evaluation Metrics](#apa-uc-metrics-reference) ### Git for Windows - [Install Git on Windows, git-scm.com](#apa-gitscm-windows-reference) - [Release 2.56.0.windows.2](#apa-gfw-release-reference) - [FAQ, supported Windows versions](#apa-gfw-faq-reference) - [32-bit support](#apa-gfw-32bit-reference) ## References Git for Windows Project. It records the gate results, a scorecard, the findings that shaped the ratings, and a recommendation for the radar. mingit passes all four default gates for personal use: it makes no network contact, holds no data, and is trivially replaced. Its problems are in how it gets onto and off a machine, and in its own correctness. The npm installer edits shell start-up files in ways that can damage them, the documented uninstall path does not work with current npm, arguments containing spaces are split apart, and one documented command fails. The licence situation is also untidy. We recommend leaving it in Assess and meeting the same need with git's own alias mechanism. ## Sources and Acknowledgements The evaluation applies *Universal Cake Evaluation Metrics* version 0.5.1 ([Steel, 2026](#apa-uc-metrics-reference)). Facts about mingit come from files in the mingit repository, read directly at commit `f893664a` on 2026-10-11, from the 2.4.0 package published on npm, from the npm registry's metadata for mingit and its dependencies, and from installing, using, and uninstalling that package under a test home directory with every relevant system call traced. The evaluation was prepared with AI assistance from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). ## Scope We evaluate mingit 2.4.0, the current release on npm, as a personal developer tool for interactive shells. No consuming project was named, and mingit is not a dependency anything else would build on, so the evaluation is scoped to a developer installing it on their own workstation. The npm install, the `g` function, and the uninstall script were tested in bash 5.2 on Linux. The zsh paths for macOS and the Oh My Zsh plugin, and the Git Bash path for Windows, were assessed from source only. mingit wraps git; it does not change what git itself does. git's own behaviour is out of scope. ## Scorecard metadata - Product or service name: mingit - Version evaluated: 2.4.0, `mingit-2.4.0.tgz` from npm, SHA-256 `0d808d5a7935922d7a96d6ad4ce20932ef76ad57bdff46d9a5554164ff5bbbe8`; repository commit `f893664a007b6bc1241c005a8427058facd5f942` - Evaluator: Christopher Steel, with AI assistance from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) - Date: 2026-10-11 - Radar ring: Assess - Test platform: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, Linux kernel 6.18, GNU bash 5.2.21, Node.js 22.22, npm 10.9.4, git 2.43 ## Gates | Gate | Result | Evidence | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Telemetry or content exposure that cannot be disabled | Pass | Verified | A trace of mingit's own install scripts recorded no network calls; every connection during `npm install` came from npm itself, fetching packages from the registry. The `g` function only calls `git`, see Findings | | A licence incompatible with the project | Pass, for use only | Verified, Inferred | `package.json` declares ISC, but the repository has no LICENSE file. The package bundles git's completion scripts, which are GPL-2.0. Using mingit raises no issue. Redistributing it inside an AGPL-3.0-or-later or GPL-3.0-or-later project would combine GPL-2.0-only code and needs licence review first, see Findings | | Failure of the accessibility floor | Pass | Inferred | A shell function with no interface of its own; all output is git's. Abbreviations reduce typing but are not self-describing. Not tested with a screen reader | | No exit | Pass | Verified | mingit holds no data. Leaving means deleting `~/.mingit.sh` and the lines it added to shell start-up files, then typing `git` again. The automated uninstall path is broken, so this exit is manual | ## Scorecard | Metric area | Rating | Evidence | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Accessibility, alternative interaction | Moderate | Inferred | Fewer keystrokes help anyone for whom typing is costly. In exchange, commands like `pll`, `psh`, and `rsto` must be memorised, and tab completion is kept, which offsets some of that. Documentation is a single README on GitHub. Not tested with assistive technology | | Multilingual integration | Moderate | Verified | Adds no messages of its own beyond install notices, so git's own localisation passes through. The abbreviations and README are English only | | Economic and cognitive accessibility | Strong | Verified | Free. The package is 289 KB unpacked, most of it bundled completion scripts and logo images; the function itself is about 1 KB. Fifteen commands to learn | | Representation | Unknown | None | Not assessable from public information. One author; no machine-learned models in the product | | Compatibility | Weak | Verified | The installer chooses by operating system, not by shell: every Linux install writes to `~/.bashrc`, so zsh and fish users on Linux are not served. Bash on macOS needs `package.json` edited before install, which is impractical for a global npm install. The Linux script hard-codes `/usr/share/bash-completion/completions/git`. The README says it was tested on Mac OS X El Capitan (claimed). Requires Node.js and npm to install a shell script | | Resilience | Strong | Verified | Works offline once installed. No services, accounts, or tokens | | Agency, sovereignty and privacy | Moderate | Verified | Stores and transmits nothing (verified). But installing it edits the user's shell start-up files without asking, and the `g` name overrides any existing `g` command or alias | | Agency, power-imbalance proxies (exit cost, portability, ToS volatility, pricing asymmetry) | Strong | Inferred | No terms, pricing, or data. Exit cost is unlearning fifteen abbreviations and removing a few lines | | Agency, interaction patterns | Weak | Verified | Not malicious, but its defaults do not respect the user's files: the install appends to `~/.bashrc` without a leading newline and without checking for an existing entry, and the documented uninstall does not run under current npm. Commands silently mis-handle arguments containing spaces. Lens: user and owner are the same person | | Environment, direct, indirect, and authoring-side | Strong | Inferred | A shell function; negligible runtime cost. Pulls five npm packages at install time to copy two files | | Security | Weak | Verified | npm install-time lifecycle scripts write to shell start-up files, a persistence location. Dependencies are declared with an empty version range, so any future release of `fs-extra` or `homedir` is accepted, and no lock file is published. `homedir` was last released in 2014 and duplicates Node's built-in `os.homedir`. No npm provenance attestation, no git tags for any release, no security policy; 119 of 123 commits are unsigned. The zsh install runs `compinit -u`, which skips zsh's check for insecure completion directories. Known advisories were not checked | | Longevity | Weak | Verified | Started in 2015. Three commits in the two years to 2026-10-11, all on 2025-06-20, and none in the last 90 days. 31 npm releases since 2016, the latest 2.4.0 in June 2025 | | Content endurance | Strong | Inferred | mingit stores and authors nothing | | Exit and portability | Moderate | Verified | No data to move, and replacements are built into git, see Findings. Exit is manual: `npm uninstall` leaves `~/.mingit.sh` and the start-up line in place, and the bundled uninstall script, run by hand, leaves a dangling line that errors on every new shell | | Adjustability and support | Moderate | Verified, Inferred | About 1 KB of shell, easy to read and change by hand. Support is GitHub issues to one person; no open issues were listed on 2026-10-11. The missing LICENSE file clouds the fork-and-fix path | | Market position (concentration, take rate, API stability, forkability, contributor concentration) | Moderate | Verified, Claimed | A small niche convenience, 79 GitHub stars and 8 forks (claimed by the GitHub page). Overlaps with git aliases and Oh My Zsh's git plugin, which its own README says it overrides. Contributor concentration: 122 of 123 commits (99%) by the author, under two name spellings; the other is one 2015 commit. No foundation-model dependency | | Gates | Pass | Mixed | All four pass for personal use. Telemetry and exit Verified; licence Verified with a redistribution caveat; accessibility floor Inferred | ## Findings ### Network and file system behaviour We installed the npm 2.4.0 package globally into a separate prefix with a test home directory, under `strace` recording `connect`, `sendto`, file opens, renames, deletions, and process starts. All 32 connections in the run came from npm's own processes, to the npm registry's address range and DNS; none came from mingit's `install.js`, `postinstall.js`, or the shell script they start. Tracing those scripts on their own confirmed it: no network calls, and exactly two writes, creating `~/.mingit.sh` and appending to `~/.bashrc`. At runtime, mingit is a shell function named `g` that maps an abbreviation to a git subcommand and passes anything else straight to `git` ([mingit Project, n.d.-c](#apa-mingit-bashrc-reference)). It has no network or storage code of its own. ### Changes to shell start-up files On Linux, the installer copies the function to `~/.mingit.sh` and appends `source ~/.mingit.sh` to `~/.bashrc` with `echo ... >>` ([mingit Project, n.d.-d](#apa-mingit-installsh-reference)). That has three consequences we reproduced. First, the append does not begin with a newline. Our test `~/.bashrc` ended with `export FOO=1` and no trailing newline, as files saved by some editors do. After install the line read `export FOO=1source ~/.mingit.sh`; a new shell set `FOO` to `1source`, printed an error, and did not load mingit. The user's own setting was silently changed. Second, the install does not check for an existing entry, so reinstalling or upgrading adds a second `source` line each time. Third, removal does not work as documented. The README notes that npm 7 and later do not run uninstall scripts ([mingit Project, n.d.-a](#apa-mingit-readme-reference)); with npm 10, `npm uninstall -g mingit` left both `~/.mingit.sh` and the `source` line in place. Running the bundled `uninstall.js` by hand, as the README suggests, deleted `~/.mingit.sh` but removed only the first `source` line ([mingit Project, n.d.-e](#apa-mingit-uninstall-reference)). After a reinstall, the remaining line made every new bash session print a "No such file or directory" error. On Windows the installer appends with no newline at all, and on macOS with zsh it appends a block that also runs `compinit -u` ([mingit Project, n.d.-b](#apa-mingit-install-reference)). These were read from source, not run. ### Correctness of the function Every case in the `g` function except `c` passes arguments as unquoted `$@`, so bash splits any argument containing a space and expands any glob. In testing, `g a "my file.txt"` ran `git add my file.txt` and failed with "pathspec 'my' did not match any files". The same applies to `g co`, `g d`, `g psh`, and the rest. The `c` case was quoted when commit was fixed, which suggests the issue is an oversight rather than a design. zsh does not split unquoted parameters by default, so zsh users are probably unaffected (inferred, not tested). The README lists `g r` for `git reset`, but the function matches `rst`; `g r` falls through to `git r`, which git rejects. The Linux manual install instruction, `cat ./.bashrc >> ~/.bashrc`, refers to a file that does not exist; the file is `scripts/bashrc`. The Windows variant lacks the completion mapping for `g f`. ### Licence The only licence statement is `"license": "ISC"` in `package.json` ([mingit Project, n.d.-f](#apa-mingit-package-reference)). The repository has no LICENSE file and GitHub shows n

Three defaults in MinGit's system configuration need a deliberate decision before the manager ships. 65 66 ## Sources and Acknowledgements 67 68 The comparison applies *Universal Cake Evaluation Metrics* version 0.5.1 ([Steel, 2026](#apa-uc-metrics-reference)). The options come from the git-scm.com Windows download page ([Git Project, n.d.](#apa-gitscm-windows-reference)) and the Git for Windows 2.56.0.2 release behind it ([Git for Windows Project, 2026](#apa-gfw-release-reference)). MinGit is exactly that, and it is published by Git for Windows itself for this purpose. The installer and winget fail the pattern by design, since they decide where things go. PortableGit fits, but carries Git Bash and much more than a manager needs, so it suits an optional "full" variant rather than the default. 91 92 dugite-native, the other candidate surveyed earlier, builds its Windows packages by repackaging MinGit. The downloaded MinGit zip hashed to `da35e72aa21c005a5a0d298cfbae110bc1609a815730ea0dde84b01a1b3cd3be`, matching the release notes (verified). The git-scm.com page itself publishes no checksums. 106 107 The table is markdown inside the release notes, not a SHA256SUMS file, so the manager must parse it, unlike osat-manager-python, which reads python-build-standalone's SHA256SUMS. GitHub's release API may report a per-asset digest, which would be simpler; that could not be checked here and should be confirmed when the manager is built. 108 109 ## Older systems 110 111 Git for Windows supports Windows 8.1 and later, on x64 and ARM64 ([Git for Windows Project, n.d.-a](#apa-gfw-faq-reference)). Older systems can only run frozen releases. 112 113 | System | Last Git for Windows release | 114 |---|---| 115 | Windows 7 and 8 | 2.46.2 | 116 | Windows Vista and Server 2008 | 2.37.1 | 117 | 32-bit, installer and PortableGit | 2.48.1 | 118 | 32-bit, MinGit only | Supported until April 2029 | 119 120 The 32-bit dates come from the project's support page ([Git for Windows Project, n.d.-b](#apa-gfw-32bit-reference)). For SAT content repositories shared between Linux and Windows, decide whether the manager keeps this default or sets `autocrlf` per repository, preferably with a `.gitattributes` policy in the repositories themselves. 136 - **Git LFS.** The same configuration declares the `lfs` filter with `required = true`, but MinGit ships no `git-lfs` executable (verified). A checkout of any repository that uses LFS will fail. The manager should either install Git LFS beside MinGit or tell the user plainly. 137 - **Inherited configuration.** MinGit's system configuration includes `C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig` and its 32-bit counterpart, so on a machine that also has a full Git for Windows install, MinGit inherits that install's settings. The manager should document this or override it. 138 - **Paths.** The 2.56 layout places Git's runtime under `ucrt64`, after a migration from `mingw64`. Aliases should target `cmd\git.exe`, the stable entry point, rather than paths inside the runtime directory. 139 140 ## Flip conditions 141 142 - If Git for Windows stops publishing 64-bit MinGit, the manager falls back to the full `tar.bz2` archive, which needs no installer either. 143 - If users mostly want Git Bash, PortableGit becomes the default and MinGit the minimal option. 144 - If checksum parsing from release notes proves fragile, and no API digest is available, verify against the signed tag by building, or pin by hash per version as osat-manager-python's archive already allows. 145 146 ## Relationship to project 147 148 This entry gives osat-manager-git its Windows half. It records the gate results, a scorecard, the findings that shaped the ratings, and a recommendation for the radar. mingit passes all four default gates for personal use: it makes no network contact, holds no data, and is trivially replaced. Its problems are in how it gets onto and off a machine, and in its own correctness. The npm installer edits shell start-up files in ways that can damage them, the documented uninstall path does not work with current npm, arguments containing spaces are split apart, and one documented command fails. The licence situation is also untidy. We recommend leaving it in Assess and meeting the same need with git's own alias mechanism. 258 259 ## Sources and Acknowledgements 260 261 The evaluation applies *Universal Cake Evaluation Metrics* version 0.5.1 ([Steel, 2026](#apa-uc-metrics-reference)). Telemetry and exit Verified; licence Verified with a redistribution caveat; accessibility floor Inferred | 308 309 ## Findings 310 311 ### Network and file system behaviour 312 313 We installed the npm 2.4.0 package globally into a separate prefix with a test home directory, under `strace` recording `connect`, `sendto`, file opens, renames, deletions, and process starts. All 32 connections in the run came from npm's own processes, to the npm registry's address range and DNS; none came from mingit's `install.js`, `postinstall.js`, or the shell script they start. Tracing those scripts on their own confirmed it: no network calls, and exactly two writes, creating `~/.mingit.sh` and appending to `~/.bashrc`. 314 315 At runtime, mingit is a shell function named `g` that maps an abbreviation to a git subcommand and passes anything else straight to `git` ([mingit Project, n.d.-c](#apa-mingit-bashrc-reference)). It has no network or storage code of its own. 316 317 ### Changes to shell start-up files 318 319 On Linux, the installer copies the function to `~/.mingit.sh` and appends `source ~/.mingit.sh` to `~/.bashrc` with `echo ... >>` ([mingit Project, n.d.-d](#apa-mingit-installsh-reference)). That has three consequences we reproduced. 320 321 First, the append does not begin with a newline. Our test `~/.bashrc` ended with `export FOO=1` and no trailing newline, as files saved by some editors do. After install the line read `export FOO=1source ~/.mingit.sh`; a new shell set `FOO` to `1source`, printed an error, and did not load mingit. The user's own setting was silently changed. 322 323 Second, the install does not check for an existing entry, so reinstalling or upgrading adds a second `source` line each time. 324 325 Third, removal does not work as documented. The README notes that npm 7 and later do not run uninstall scripts ([mingit Project, n.d.-a](#apa-mingit-readme-reference)); with npm 10, `npm uninstall -g mingit` left both `~/.mingit.sh` and the `source` line in place. Running the bundled `uninstall.js` by hand, as the README suggests, deleted `~/.mingit.sh` but removed only the first `source` line ([mingit Project, n.d.-e](#apa-mingit-uninstall-reference)). After a reinstall, the remaining line made every new bash session print a "No such file or directory" error. 326 327 On Windows the installer appends with no newline at all, and on macOS with zsh it appends a block that also runs `compinit -u` ([mingit Project, n.d.-b](#apa-mingit-install-reference)). These were read from source, not run. 328 329 ### Correctness of the function 330 331 Every case in the `g` function except `c` passes arguments as unquoted `$@`, so bash splits any argument containing a space and expands any glob. In testing, `g a "my file.txt"` ran `git add my file.txt` and failed with "pathspec 'my' did not match any files". The same applies to `g co`, `g d`, `g psh`, and the rest. The `c` case was quoted when commit was fixed, which suggests the issue is an oversight rather than a design. zsh does not split unquoted parameters by default, so zsh users are probably unaffected (inferred, not tested). 332 333 The README lists `g r` for `git reset`, but the function matches `rst`; `g r` falls through to `git r`, which git rejects. The Linux manual install instruction, `cat ./.bashrc >> ~/.bashrc`, refers to a file that does not exist; the file is `scripts/bashrc`. The Windows variant lacks the completion mapping for `g f`. 334 335 ### Licence 336 337 The only licence statement is `"license": "ISC"` in `package.json` ([mingit Project, n.d.-f](#apa-mingit-package-reference)). The repository has no LICENSE file and GitHub shows no detected licence. ISC requires its copyright and permission notice to accompany copies, and without the text there is no notice to carry, so the grant rests on a metadata field. 338 339 The package also bundles copies of git's bash completion script and zsh completion wrapper, plus an older bash-completion library inside `scripts/bash_profile`. The bash script's header says it is distributed under GPL version 2.0 ([mingit Project, n.d.-g](#apa-mingit-completion-reference)), and git as a whole is GPL-2.0-only. None of this matters for running mingit. It does matter for redistribution: an ISC label over a package that contains GPL-2.0 files misstates the package's terms, and GPL-2.0-only code cannot be combined into an AGPL-3.0-or-later or GPL-3.0-or-later work. Anyone shipping mingit inside a Vishpala project should drop the bundled completion scripts and rely on the system's copy, which the Linux variant already does. 340 341 ### Supply chain and maintenance 342 343 The npm package's code files match the repository at `f893664a` byte for byte. The package also contains IDE configuration directories, `.idea` and `.vscode`, that are not in the repository, which shows it was published from the author's working copy rather than from a clean checkout or CI. There are no git tags, so a version can only be matched to a commit by comparing contents, as we did. npm holds a registry signature for 2.4.0 but no provenance attestation ([mingit Project, 2025](#apa-mingit-npm-reference)). 344 345 The two runtime dependencies are declared with empty version strings, which npm treats as "any version", and the lock file is in `.gitignore`. Our install resolved `fs-extra` 11.4.1 and `homedir` 0.6.0. `homedir` was last published in 2014 ([Moore, 2014](#apa-homedir-npm-reference)) and does what Node's built-in `os.homedir` has done for years. A shell script that needs to copy two files does not need either package, and every install fetches whatever their maintainers have most recently published. 346 347 Activity is low. Of 123 commits since July 2015, 122 are by the author; the three in the last two years were made on a single day in June 2025, adding `g dst` and updating the README. 348 349 ### Replacement path 350 351 git provides the same capability without an installer. `git config --global alias.s status`, and similar lines for each abbreviation, give `git s` with full completion and correct argument handling. For a one-letter `g`, bash's git completion provides `__git_complete g git`, to be run after `alias g=git` (verified in bash 5.2 with git 2.43) ([Git Project, n.d.](#apa-git-completion-reference)). Both live in files the user already controls, can be kept in a dotfiles repository, and involve no third-party code. 352 353 ## Recommendation 354 355 Keep mingit in Assess and do not move it to Trial. For the need it addresses, prefer git's own aliases, set in `~/.gitconfig` or a managed dotfiles repository, with `__git_complete` for a one-letter wrapper. 356 357 If mingit itself is wanted on a workstation: 358 359 - Do not install it through npm. Copy the relevant function file by hand, and add the `source` line yourself. 360 - Quote `"$@"` throughout the function before use, and remove the `g r` line from any notes. 361 - Back up shell start-up files before installing, and check them afterwards. 362 - To remove an npm install, delete `~/.mingit.sh` and every `source ~/.mingit.sh` line by hand, and check the line before each for a missing newline. 363 - Do not redistribute it in any project until it has a LICENSE file and the bundled GPL-2.0 completion scripts are removed. 364 365 Worth reporting upstream: the missing leading newline on append, duplicate entries on reinstall, the unquoted `$@`, the `g r` mismatch, the manual install path, the missing LICENSE file, the bundled GPL-2.0 files under an ISC label, and the unpinned dependencies. 366 367 Re-review triggers specific to mingit: a LICENSE file added, an install method that no longer runs npm lifecycle scripts or that edits start-up files safely, or renewed maintenance activity. 368 369 ## License 370 371 This document, *Universal Cake Evaluation: mingit, Git Command Alias*, by **Christopher Steel**, with AI assistance from **Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)**, is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html). 372 373 ## Resources 374 375 ### Evaluation framework 376 377 - It recommends MinGit, taken directly from Git for Windows releases, as the manager's source, and the standard installer for client machines that a person will use directly. The git-scm.com download page does not list MinGit, so the recommendation rests on the release itself, whose checksums and signed tag make it verifiable. Three defaults in MinGit's system configuration need a deliberate decision before the manager ships. ## Sources and Acknowledgements The comparison applies *Universal Cake Evaluation Metrics* version 0.5.1 ([Steel, 2026](#apa-uc-metrics-reference)). The options come from the git-scm.com Windows download page ([Git Project, n.d.](#apa-gitscm-windows-reference)) and the Git for Windows 2.56.0.2 release behind it ([Git for Windows Project, 2026](#apa-gfw-release-reference)). Support periods come from the Git for Windows FAQ and its 32-bit support page. `MinGit-2.56.0.2-64-bit.zip` was downloaded, hashed, and unpacked on Linux to inspect its layout and configuration; no Windows binary was run. The evaluation was prepared with AI assistance from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). ## Scope The subject is Git for Windows 2.56.0.2, released on 2026-10-05, in each of the forms it is offered. Git's own behaviour, and Git on Linux and macOS, are out of scope; for those platforms, dugite-native remains the candidate, pending its own entry. Network behaviour and accessibility of the Windows builds were not tested, since nothing was run on Windows. ## The options | Option | Artifact | What it is | Use | |---|---|---|---| | MinGit | `MinGit-2.56.0.2-64-bit.zip`, also ARM64 and 32-bit | Git for Windows' minimal build for applications that bundle Git: `git.exe` and its helpers, Git Credential Manager, no Bash, no GUI tools. 39.8 MB zip, 93 MB unpacked (verified) | osat-manager-git | | MinGit, busybox variant | `MinGit-2.56.0.2-busybox-64-bit.zip`, also ARM64 and 32-bit | MinGit with BusyBox in place of the standard Unix tools; smaller, less compatible | None | | PortableGit | `PortableGit-2.56.0.2-64-bit.7z.exe`, also ARM64 | Full Git for Windows, including Git Bash, unpacked into any folder with no registry or PATH changes; a self-extracting 7-Zip archive that 7-Zip can open without running it | Optional full variant for the manager | | Full archive | `Git-2.56.0.2-64-bit.tar.bz2`, also ARM64 | The full Git as a plain archive | Alternative to PortableGit | | Standalone installer | `Git-2.56.0.2-64-bit.exe`, also ARM64 | Full Git for Windows with Git Bash, Git GUI, gitk, Explorer menus, and PATH changes | Client machines, git-cola | | winget | `winget install --id Git.Git -e --source winget` | The standalone installer, through Microsoft's package manager | Client setup where winget is present | | Build from source | Git for Windows repository | Compile it yourself | None | The git-scm.com page lists only the installer, PortableGit, winget, and source. MinGit, its busybox variants, and the full archives appear only on the release. ## The decisive observation The osat-manager pattern needs an artifact it can download, verify against a published checksum, unpack into a versioned directory, and point an alias at, with no installer and no system changes. MinGit is exactly that, and it is published by Git for Windows itself for this purpose. The installer and winget fail the pattern by design, since they decide where things go. PortableGit fits, but carries Git Bash and much more than a manager needs, so it suits an optional "full" variant rather than the default. dugite-native, the other candidate surveyed earlier, builds its Windows packages by repackaging MinGit. Taking MinGit at its source removes GitHub Desktop's packaging from the Windows dependency chain without losing anything. ## Gates for Git for Windows | Gate | Result | Evidence | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Telemetry or content exposure that cannot be disabled | Pass | Inferred | Git has no telemetry. Git Credential Manager contacts a hosting service only when credentials are requested for it. Not traced on Windows | | A licence incompatible with the project | Pass, for use | Verified | Git is GPL-2.0-only; the bundled `LICENSE.txt` states that only version 2 applies. Using MinGit raises no issue, and redistributing it carries the GPL's usual source obligations; Git's code cannot be combined into AGPL-3.0-or-later or GPL-3.0-or-later works | | Failure of the accessibility floor | Pass | Inferred | MinGit is a command-line tool with no interface of its own. The installer's accessibility was not tested | | No exit | Pass | Verified | Repositories are plain Git. Removing MinGit means deleting its directory | ## Verification The release notes carry a SHA-256 table covering every asset, the release tag is GPG-signed by the Git for Windows maintainer, and the executables carry Authenticode signatures (claimed by the release page). The downloaded MinGit zip hashed to `da35e72aa21c005a5a0d298cfbae110bc1609a815730ea0dde84b01a1b3cd3be`, matching the release notes (verified). The git-scm.com page itself publishes no checksums. The table is markdown inside the release notes, not a SHA256SUMS file, so the manager must parse it, unlike osat-manager-python, which reads python-build-standalone's SHA256SUMS. GitHub's release API may report a per-asset digest, which would be simpler; that could not be checked here and should be confirmed when the manager is built. ## Older systems Git for Windows supports Windows 8.1 and later, on x64 and ARM64 ([Git for Windows Project, n.d.-a](#apa-gfw-faq-reference)). Older systems can only run frozen releases. | System | Last Git for Windows release | |---|---| | Windows 7 and 8 | 2.46.2 | | Windows Vista and Server 2008 | 2.37.1 | | 32-bit, installer and PortableGit | 2.48.1 | | 32-bit, MinGit only | Supported until April 2029 | The 32-bit dates come from the project's support page ([Git for Windows Project, n.d.-b](#apa-gfw-32bit-reference)). A manager could pin 2.46.2 for a Windows 7 client, as the psutil entry suggests pinning 7.2.x for older Python, but that machine gets no further Git security fixes. Client-facing guidance should say so plainly. ## Recommendation | Option | Ring | For | |---|---|---| | MinGit, from Git for Windows releases | Trial | osat-manager-git's Windows source | | PortableGit | Assess | An optional full variant of the manager, for users who want Git Bash | | Standalone installer, or winget | Assess | Client machines a person uses directly, and git-cola, whose README asks for it | | MinGit busybox variants | Hold | Less compatible, no offsetting benefit | | Building from source | Hold | The official builds already meet the need | | Frozen releases for Windows 7, 8, or Vista | Hold | Only as a declared bridge, with the security cost stated | MinGit moves to Adopt when osat-manager-git installs, switches, and removes it end to end on real Windows hardware, with these decisions made and recorded in its proposal: - **Line endings.** MinGit's system configuration sets `core.autocrlf = true`. For SAT content repositories shared between Linux and Windows, decide whether the manager keeps this default or sets `autocrlf` per repository, preferably with a `.gitattributes` policy in the repositories themselves. - **Git LFS.** The same configuration declares the `lfs` filter with `required = true`, but MinGit ships no `git-lfs` executable (verified). A checkout of any repository that uses LFS will fail. The manager should either install Git LFS beside MinGit or tell the user plainly. - **Inherited configuration.** MinGit's system configuration includes `C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig` and its 32-bit counterpart, so on a machine that also has a full Git for Windows install, MinGit inherits that install's settings. The manager should document this or override it. - **Paths.** The 2.56 layout places Git's runtime under `ucrt64`, after a migration from `mingw64`. Aliases should target `cmd\git.exe`, the stable entry point, rather than paths inside the runtime directory. ## Flip conditions - If Git for Windows stops publishing 64-bit MinGit, the manager falls back to the full `tar.bz2` archive, which needs no installer either. - If users mostly want Git Bash, PortableGit becomes the default and MinGit the minimal option. - If checksum parsing from release notes proves fragile, and no API digest is available, verify against the signed tag by building, or pin by hash per version as osat-manager-python's archive already allows. ## Relationship to project This entry gives osat-manager-git its Windows half. On Linux and macOS the candidate remains dugite-native, whose builds need relocation variables in the alias wrapper, link the system's libcurl for HTTPS, and require glibc 2.34; that candidate needs its own entry. git-cola, evaluated separately, needs Git on the path and would be a natural consumer of the manager. ## Status notes - Last reviewed: 2026-10-11 - In assess: the automated pass recommends MinGit for Trial as the manager's Windows source. What moves it to Adopt is the manager working end to end on real Windows, with the four decisions above recorded in its proposal. - Re-review triggers: a change in how Git for Windows publishes checksums, any change to MinGit's default system configuration, and the end of 32-bit MinGit in April 2029. ## License This document, *Git on Windows, Options for osat-manager-git*, by **Christopher Steel**, with AI assistance from **Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)**, is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html). ## Resources ### Evaluation framework - [Universal Cake Evaluation Metrics](#apa-uc-metrics-reference) ### Git for Windows - [Install Git on Windows, git-scm.com](#apa-gitscm-windows-reference) - [Release 2.56.0.windows.2](#apa-gfw-release-reference) - [FAQ, supported Windows versions](#apa-gfw-faq-reference) - [32-bit support](#apa-gfw-32bit-reference) ## References Git for Windows Project. It records the gate results, a scorecard, the findings that shaped the ratings, and a recommendation for the radar. mingit passes all four default gates for personal use: it makes no network contact, holds no data, and is trivially replaced. Its problems are in how it gets onto and off a machine, and in its own correctness. The npm installer edits shell start-up files in ways that can damage them, the documented uninstall path does not work with current npm, arguments containing spaces are split apart, and one documented command fails. The licence situation is also untidy. We recommend leaving it in Assess and meeting the same need with git's own alias mechanism. ## Sources and Acknowledgements The evaluation applies *Universal Cake Evaluation Metrics* version 0.5.1 ([Steel, 2026](#apa-uc-metrics-reference)). Facts about mingit come from files in the mingit repository, read directly at commit `f893664a` on 2026-10-11, from the 2.4.0 package published on npm, from the npm registry's metadata for mingit and its dependencies, and from installing, using, and uninstalling that package under a test home directory with every relevant system call traced. The evaluation was prepared with AI assistance from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). ## Scope We evaluate mingit 2.4.0, the current release on npm, as a personal developer tool for interactive shells. No consuming project was named, and mingit is not a dependency anything else would build on, so the evaluation is scoped to a developer installing it on their own workstation. The npm install, the `g` function, and the uninstall script were tested in bash 5.2 on Linux. The zsh paths for macOS and the Oh My Zsh plugin, and the Git Bash path for Windows, were assessed from source only. mingit wraps git; it does not change what git itself does. git's own behaviour is out of scope. ## Scorecard metadata - Product or service name: mingit - Version evaluated: 2.4.0, `mingit-2.4.0.tgz` from npm, SHA-256 `0d808d5a7935922d7a96d6ad4ce20932ef76ad57bdff46d9a5554164ff5bbbe8`; repository commit `f893664a007b6bc1241c005a8427058facd5f942` - Evaluator: Christopher Steel, with AI assistance from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) - Date: 2026-10-11 - Radar ring: Assess - Test platform: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, Linux kernel 6.18, GNU bash 5.2.21, Node.js 22.22, npm 10.9.4, git 2.43 ## Gates | Gate | Result | Evidence | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Telemetry or content exposure that cannot be disabled | Pass | Verified | A trace of mingit's own install scripts recorded no network calls; every connection during `npm install` came from npm itself, fetching packages from the registry. The `g` function only calls `git`, see Findings | | A licence incompatible with the project | Pass, for use only | Verified, Inferred | `package.json` declares ISC, but the repository has no LICENSE file. The package bundles git's completion scripts, which are GPL-2.0. Using mingit raises no issue. Redistributing it inside an AGPL-3.0-or-later or GPL-3.0-or-later project would combine GPL-2.0-only code and needs licence review first, see Findings | | Failure of the accessibility floor | Pass | Inferred | A shell function with no interface of its own; all output is git's. Abbreviations reduce typing but are not self-describing. Not tested with a screen reader | | No exit | Pass | Verified | mingit holds no data. Leaving means deleting `~/.mingit.sh` and the lines it added to shell start-up files, then typing `git` again. The automated uninstall path is broken, so this exit is manual | ## Scorecard | Metric area | Rating | Evidence | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Accessibility, alternative interaction | Moderate | Inferred | Fewer keystrokes help anyone for whom typing is costly. In exchange, commands like `pll`, `psh`, and `rsto` must be memorised, and tab completion is kept, which offsets some of that. Documentation is a single README on GitHub. Not tested with assistive technology | | Multilingual integration | Moderate | Verified | Adds no messages of its own beyond install notices, so git's own localisation passes through. The abbreviations and README are English only | | Economic and cognitive accessibility | Strong | Verified | Free. The package is 289 KB unpacked, most of it bundled completion scripts and logo images; the function itself is about 1 KB. Fifteen commands to learn | | Representation | Unknown | None | Not assessable from public information. One author; no machine-learned models in the product | | Compatibility | Weak | Verified | The installer chooses by operating system, not by shell: every Linux install writes to `~/.bashrc`, so zsh and fish users on Linux are not served. Bash on macOS needs `package.json` edited before install, which is impractical for a global npm install. The Linux script hard-codes `/usr/share/bash-completion/completions/git`. The README says it was tested on Mac OS X El Capitan (claimed). Requires Node.js and npm to install a shell script | | Resilience | Strong | Verified | Works offline once installed. No services, accounts, or tokens | | Agency, sovereignty and privacy | Moderate | Verified | Stores and transmits nothing (verified). But installing it edits the user's shell start-up files without asking, and the `g` name overrides any existing `g` command or alias | | Agency, power-imbalance proxies (exit cost, portability, ToS volatility, pricing asymmetry) | Strong | Inferred | No terms, pricing, or data. Exit cost is unlearning fifteen abbreviations and removing a few lines | | Agency, interaction patterns | Weak | Verified | Not malicious, but its defaults do not respect the user's files: the install appends to `~/.bashrc` without a leading newline and without checking for an existing entry, and the documented uninstall does not run under current npm. Commands silently mis-handle arguments containing spaces. Lens: user and owner are the same person | | Environment, direct, indirect, and authoring-side | Strong | Inferred | A shell function; negligible runtime cost. Pulls five npm packages at install time to copy two files | | Security | Weak | Verified | npm install-time lifecycle scripts write to shell start-up files, a persistence location. Dependencies are declared with an empty version range, so any future release of `fs-extra` or `homedir` is accepted, and no lock file is published. `homedir` was last released in 2014 and duplicates Node's built-in `os.homedir`. No npm provenance attestation, no git tags for any release, no security policy; 119 of 123 commits are unsigned. The zsh install runs `compinit -u`, which skips zsh's check for insecure completion directories. Known advisories were not checked | | Longevity | Weak | Verified | Started in 2015. Three commits in the two years to 2026-10-11, all on 2025-06-20, and none in the last 90 days. 31 npm releases since 2016, the latest 2.4.0 in June 2025 | | Content endurance | Strong | Inferred | mingit stores and authors nothing | | Exit and portability | Moderate | Verified | No data to move, and replacements are built into git, see Findings. Exit is manual: `npm uninstall` leaves `~/.mingit.sh` and the start-up line in place, and the bundled uninstall script, run by hand, leaves a dangling line that errors on every new shell | | Adjustability and support | Moderate | Verified, Inferred | About 1 KB of shell, easy to read and change by hand. Support is GitHub issues to one person; no open issues were listed on 2026-10-11. The missing LICENSE file clouds the fork-and-fix path | | Market position (concentration, take rate, API stability, forkability, contributor concentration) | Moderate | Verified, Claimed | A small niche convenience, 79 GitHub stars and 8 forks (claimed by the GitHub page). Overlaps with git aliases and Oh My Zsh's git plugin, which its own README says it overrides. Contributor concentration: 122 of 123 commits (99%) by the author, under two name spellings; the other is one 2015 commit. No foundation-model dependency | | Gates | Pass | Mixed | All four pass for personal use. Telemetry and exit Verified; licence Verified with a redistribution caveat; accessibility floor Inferred | ## Findings ### Network and file system behaviour We installed the npm 2.4.0 package globally into a separate prefix with a test home directory, under `strace` recording `connect`, `sendto`, file opens, renames, deletions, and process starts. All 32 connections in the run came from npm's own processes, to the npm registry's address range and DNS; none came from mingit's `install.js`, `postinstall.js`, or the shell script they start. Tracing those scripts on their own confirmed it: no network calls, and exactly two writes, creating `~/.mingit.sh` and appending to `~/.bashrc`. At runtime, mingit is a shell function named `g` that maps an abbreviation to a git subcommand and passes anything else straight to `git` ([mingit Project, n.d.-c](#apa-mingit-bashrc-reference)). It has no network or storage code of its own. ### Changes to shell start-up files On Linux, the installer copies the function to `~/.mingit.sh` and appends `source ~/.mingit.sh` to `~/.bashrc` with `echo ... >>` ([mingit Project, n.d.-d](#apa-mingit-installsh-reference)). That has three consequences we reproduced. First, the append does not begin with a newline. Our test `~/.bashrc` ended with `export FOO=1` and no trailing newline, as files saved by some editors do. After install the line read `export FOO=1source ~/.mingit.sh`; a new shell set `FOO` to `1source`, printed an error, and did not load mingit. The user's own setting was silently changed. Second, the install does not check for an existing entry, so reinstalling or upgrading adds a second `source` line each time. Third, removal does not work as documented. The README notes that npm 7 and later do not run uninstall scripts ([mingit Project, n.d.-a](#apa-mingit-readme-reference)); with npm 10, `npm uninstall -g mingit` left both `~/.mingit.sh` and the `source` line in place. Running the bundled `uninstall.js` by hand, as the README suggests, deleted `~/.mingit.sh` but removed only the first `source` line ([mingit Project, n.d.-e](#apa-mingit-uninstall-reference)). After a reinstall, the remaining line made every new bash session print a "No such file or directory" error. On Windows the installer appends with no newline at all, and on macOS with zsh it appends a block that also runs `compinit -u` ([mingit Project, n.d.-b](#apa-mingit-install-reference)). These were read from source, not run. ### Correctness of the function Every case in the `g` function except `c` passes arguments as unquoted `$@`, so bash splits any argument containing a space and expands any glob. In testing, `g a "my file.txt"` ran `git add my file.txt` and failed with "pathspec 'my' did not match any files". The same applies to `g co`, `g d`, `g psh`, and the rest. The `c` case was quoted when commit was fixed, which suggests the issue is an oversight rather than a design. zsh does not split unquoted parameters by default, so zsh users are probably unaffected (inferred, not tested). The README lists `g r` for `git reset`, but the function matches `rst`; `g r` falls through to `git r`, which git rejects. The Linux manual install instruction, `cat ./.bashrc >> ~/.bashrc`, refers to a file that does not exist; the file is `scripts/bashrc`. The Windows variant lacks the completion mapping for `g f`. ### Licence The only licence statement is `"license": "ISC"` in `package.json` ([mingit Project, n.d.-f](#apa-mingit-package-reference)). The repository has no LICENSE file and GitHub shows no detected licence. ISC requires its copyright and permission notice to accompany copies, and without the text there is no notice to carry, so the grant rests on a metadata field. The package also bundles copies of git's bash completion script and zsh completion wrapper, plus an older bash-completion library inside `scripts/bash_profile`. The bash script's header says it is distributed under GPL version 2.0 ([mingit Project, n.d.-g](#apa-mingit-completion-reference)), and git as a whole is GPL-2.0-only. None of this matters for running mingit. It does matter for redistribution: an ISC label over a package that contains GPL-2.0 files misstates the package's terms, and GPL-2.0-only code cannot be combined into an AGPL-3.0-or-later or GPL-3.0-or-later work. Anyone shipping mingit inside a Vishpala project should drop the bundled completion scripts and rely on the system's copy, which the Linux variant already does. ### Supply chain and maintenance The npm package's code files match the repository at `f893664a` byte for byte. The package also contains IDE configuration directories, `.idea` and `.vscode`, that are not in the repository, which shows it was published from the author's working copy rather than from a clean checkout or CI. There are no git tags, so a version can only be matched to a commit by comparing contents, as we did. npm holds a registry signature for 2.4.0 but no provenance attestation ([mingit Project, 2025](#apa-mingit-npm-reference)). The two runtime dependencies are declared with empty version strings, which npm treats as "any version", and the lock file is in `.gitignore`. Our install resolved `fs-extra` 11.4.1 and `homedir` 0.6.0. `homedir` was last published in 2014 ([Moore, 2014](#apa-homedir-npm-reference)) and does what Node's built-in `os.homedir` has done for years. A shell script that needs to copy two files does not need either package, and every install fetches whatever their maintainers have most recently published. Activity is low. Of 123 commits since July 2015, 122 are by the author; the three in the last two years were made on a single day in June 2025, adding `g dst` and updating the README. ### Replacement path git provides the same capability without an installer. `git config --global alias.s status`, and similar lines for each abbreviation, give `git s` with full completion and correct argument handling. For a one-letter `g`, bash's git completion provides `__git_complete g git`, to be run after `alias g=git` (verified in bash 5.2 with git 2.43) ([Git Project, n.d.](#apa-git-completion-reference)). Both live in files the user already controls, can be kept in a dotfiles repository, and involve no third-party code. ## Recommendation Keep mingit in Assess and do not move it to Trial. For the need it addresses, prefer git's own aliases, set in `~/.gitconfig` or a managed dotfiles repository, with `__git_complete` for a one-letter wrapper. If mingit itself is wanted on a workstation: - Do not install it through npm. Copy the relevant function file by hand, and add the `source` line yourself. - Quote `"$@"` throughout the function before use, and remove the `g r` line from any notes. - Back up shell start-up files before installing, and check them afterwards. - To remove an npm install, delete `~/.mingit.sh` and every `source ~/.mingit.sh` line by hand, and check the line before each for a missing newline. - Do not redistribute it in any project until it has a LICENSE file and the bundled GPL-2.0 completion scripts are removed. Worth reporting upstream: the missing leading newline on append, duplicate entries on reinstall, the unquoted `$@`, the `g r` mismatch, the manual install path, the missing LICENSE file, the bundled GPL-2.0 files under an ISC label, and the unpinned dependencies. Re-review triggers specific to mingit: a LICENSE file added, an install method that no longer runs npm lifecycle scripts or that edits start-up files safely, or renewed maintenance activity. ## License This document, *Universal Cake Evaluation: mingit, Git Command Alias*, by **Christopher Steel**, with AI assistance from **Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)**, is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html). ## Resources ### Evaluation framework - [Universal Cake Evaluation Metrics](#apa-uc-metrics-reference) ### mingit repository - [README](#apa-mingit-readme-reference) - [Install script, install.js](#apa-mingit-install-reference) - [Linux function, scripts/bashrc](#apa-mingit-bashrc-reference) - [Linux install script](#apa-mingit-installsh-reference) - [Uninstall script](#apa-mingit-uninstall-reference) - [package.json](#apa-mingit-package-reference) - [Bundled git completion script](#apa-mingit-completion-reference) ### Packages and replacements - [mingit 2.4.0 on npm](#apa-mingit-npm-reference) - [homedir on npm](#apa-homedir-npm-reference) - [git-completion.bash](#apa-git-completion-reference) ## References Git Project. entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

The search turned up mostly prefix.dev and rattler-build material. Nothing I found confirms that conda-forge itself signs all its packages with Sigstore.

- **Standard:** Sigstore attestations for conda packages follow CEP-27, which uses the in-toto attestation format with a conda-specific predicate. The predicate includes the package's SHA256 hash, the full filename, and optionally the target channel URL.
- **Provenance:** Per the prefix.dev announcement, the attestation links the package producer, such as a GitHub Actions workflow, to the uploaded artifact, and trusted publishing makes this verifiable.
- **Transparency log:** Metadata about the artifact is recorded in a transparency log that can be inspected at any time.
- **Tooling:** rattler-build can generate these attestations; its docs describe a --generate-attestation flag used when publishing to prefix.dev.
- **Status:** prefix.dev announced that Sigstore support is in public beta. Its blog also says the work was done under the Conda Enhancement Proposal 27.

For conda-forge specifically, I'd check its own documentation or the conda-forge security blog, since these results don't cover it directly.

Entire is Thomas Dohmke's developer platform for AI coding agents. It launched on February 10, 2026, with a $60 million seed round at a $300 million valuation, led by Felicis, with participation from Madrona, M12, and Basis Set.

Its first product is Checkpoints, an open-source command-line tool. It attaches the agent's session to each Git commit. Coverage differs on how far that has progressed. One profile says the full platform hasn't launched yet, and no commercial pricing has been announced as of June 2026. Another notes that only Checkpoints is publicly available so far.

Launch reception was mixed. One profile reports that the HN thread drew heavy skepticism about whether checkpoint data is something developers actually want.

The mise conda backend lets you install conda-forge packages without conda, mamba, or micromamba on your machine. Its official docs say the backend downloads and extracts packages directly from anaconda.org. Usage is like mise use -g conda:ruff, with a default channel of conda-forge that you can override per package, for example with bioconda.

Key points from the results:

- **Introduction:** The conda backend first appeared in the 2025.11.11 release, which added support for installing packages from conda-forge (per a third-party installer page that mirrors the release notes).
- **Maturity:** The 2026.5.0 release graduated the conda backend out of experimental.
- **Locking:** Release 2026.1.4 added dependency locking for reproducible conda installs and fixed hardcoded library paths in conda packages (per the release notes on newreleases.io).
- **PATH fix:** Release 2026.3.7 fixed conda packages that cluttered PATH with dozens of transitive dependency binaries (per the same third-party installer page).
- **Platforms:** The backend picks the right build for your OS and architecture and falls back to noarch packages when no platform build exists.

The official docs page is the best primary source. The silentinstallhq pages are third-party mirrors, so I'd check the GitHub release notes for exact details.

toolu_0143vmxr2J7heLJvBBk7qiDz.prompt: Describe exactly how the conda backend works: where it downloads from, how it resolves dependencies, how it verifies packages (checksums, signatures), how it handles prefix replacement / relocation and macOS code signing, lockfile support, Windows support, and stated limitations. Quote details.

content.content:
**Download source:** By default, packages come from `conda-forge`, set by `conda.channel` (env var `MISE_CONDA_CHANNEL`). A tool can use a different channel with the `channel` option, which accepts an anaconda.org channel name or a full URL such as `https://conda.example.com/my-team`. To fetch through a mirror, you map the URL with `url_replacements`. mise "applies the replacements to channel metadata and package downloads" and refuses a replacement that would send credentials from an `https://` URL to an `http://` one.

**Dependency resolution:** mise solves and downloads packages itself, so conda, mamba, and micromamba are not needed. Each tool gets its own isolated prefix with one package and its dependencies. The solver also considers `noarch` packages, though a `noarch` package may depend on platform-specific packages. Solving uses only the one selected channel, so the package and all its dependencies must come from it. This is why channels that build on conda-forge, such as bioconda, usually can't be used alone. mise does not read or maintain an `environment.yml`.

**Platform selection:** mise picks the conda subdir for the host: `linux-64`, `linux-aarch64`, `osx-64`, `osx-arm64`, or `win-64`. Host-native requirements, such as a compatible libc or GPU driver, still come from the host.

**Command execution:** Only the requested package's commands go on `PATH`, not its dependencies'. If the prefix needs activation, mise runs commands through a launcher that sets `CONDA_PREFIX`, puts the prefix's executables first on `PATH`, and runs the `etc/conda/activate.d` scripts. Single-binary packages such as `conda:ripgrep` are symlinked directly on Unix. Those commands don't see `CONDA_PREFIX`.

**Windows:** Windows x64 (`win-64`) is supported. The page says "On Windows every command goes through a launcher."

**Not covered by the page:**
- **Checksums and signatures:** The page does not say how packages are verified.
- **Prefix relocation:** Not described.
- **macOS code signing:** Not described.
- **Lockfiles:** Not mentioned. The only config-file behavior described is the `[tools]` entry written by `mise use`.

**Stated limitations:**
- Commands from dependencies are not placed on `PATH`.
- `noarch` packages are not guaranteed to install on every host.
- Native requirements come from the host.
- Packages must exist for the platform in the selected channel, or they are unavailable.
- Multi-channel setups like bioconda-on-conda-forge are generally unsupported.

For verification, relocation, and lockfile details, check the implementation in `src/backend/conda.rs` on GitHub.

content.content:
**Entire: products and services listed on the page**

- **Git hosting** ("The fastest Git network on Earth"): Hosts Git repositories and mirrors them globally. The page claims agents can clone and push up to 89 times faster than competitors, based on its forgemark benchmark (418 pushes/sec vs. GitHub's 4.7). Pricing: not stated. Open source: not stated. Supported agents: not stated. Storage: hosted, with regional options (below). Hosted: yes. URL: https://entire.io
- **Multi-region code hosting**: Keeps code resident in chosen regions, "available today" in India, Australia, the EU, and the US. A "decentralized everywhere" option is marked "SOON." Pricing: not stated. Storage: the region you select. Hosted: yes.
- **Session storage**: Captures agent conversations and links them to commits as "checkpoints," so each commit ties to the reasoning behind it. The page says secrets are detected and redacted before storage. Pricing: not stated. Storage: the page is ambiguous. The headline says sessions are "stored in your repo," while the body says Entire stores code and sessions, so the exact location isn't clear. Hosted: implied.
- **Semantic Graph** (`entire-graph`, https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph): A codebase-understanding layer meant to cut token use by up to 71%. It runs 100% locally. Open source: yes, but the licence isn't named on the page. Pricing: free as described. Benchmark: 94.74% accuracy on LoCoMo across 1,540 questions. Storage: local. Hosted: no.
- **Agentic Search**: One query across repositories, commits, and agent sessions. Pricing: not stated. Open source: not stated. Storage: not stated. Hosted: implied.
- **Entire CLI** (https://github.com/entireio/cli, install via `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`): The page says "All features are available through the CLI." Open source: yes, MIT licence, with about 5.2K GitHub stars. Pricing: not stated. Supported agents: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and Cursor. Storage: follows the session and hosting options above. Hosted: no, it's a local tool.
- **forgemark** (https://github.com/entireio/forgemark): An open source Git benchmark used for the speed comparison. Licence: not stated.
- **Rebellion** (https://entire.io/rebellion): A mailing list and community offering developer news, early access, and exclusive drops. Pricing: not stated.

**Pricing and plans:** The page lists no pricing or plan tiers. Its only call to action is "Get Started" (https://entire.io/login).

3:Entire hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions as you work. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written in your repo.
8:- **Pick up where you left off** — resume an agent session and its conversation from a checkpoint
9:- **Keep Git history clean** — agent context lives outside your branch's history
16:- **Resume from any checkpoint** — Go back to any previous agent session and pick up exactly where you or a coworker left off.
